correctness.rationale: The commutator induces the standard nondegenerate \(\mathbb F_q\)-symplectic form on \(V=H_n(q)/Z\). For any subgroup \(K\ge Z\), its image \(U\) is an \(\mathbb F_p\)-subspace and its centralizer depends only on the \(\mathbb F_q\)-span \(S=\langle U\rangle_q\), giving \(|C_G(K)|=q^{1+2n-\dim_q S}\). Writing \(q=p^f\), \(s=\dim_p U\), \(d=\dim_qS\), one gets \(m_G(K)=q^{2n+2}p^{s-fd}\le q^{2n+2}\), with equality exactly when \(U\) is already \(\mathbb F_q\)-linear. Adjoining \(Z\) only increases the measure, so these are all maximizers. Every \(\mathbb F_q\)-subspace occurs as a centralizer via symplectic orthogonal complement, proving both lattice identifications. For \(q=p\), every subgroup above \(Z\) has field-linear image, giving \(\mathcal{CD}(G)=[G/Z]\) and hence full-lattice monotonicity by the known criterion; for \(f>1\), the subgroup with image \(\mathbb F_p v\) gives a strict measure drop and disproves monotonicity. The inspected verifier exhaustively checks additive subspaces for \((n,q)=(2,2),(2,3),(1,4)\).

value.rationale: The finite Heisenberg groups are canonical class-two groups, and the Chermak--Delgado lattice is a standard structural invariant. Identifying it uniformly with the full finite-field subspace lattice, plus the exact prime-versus-prime-power monotonicity transition, gives a natural complete family classification extending the known rank-one quasi-antichain picture.

final_claim: For the finite Heisenberg group \(H_n(q)\), the centralizer lattice and Chermak--Delgado lattice are exactly the inverse images of the \(\mathbb F_q\)-subspaces of \(H_n(q)/Z\), hence are canonically \(L_{2n}(q)\); the maximal Chermak--Delgado measure is \(q^{2n+2}\). The measure is increasing on the centralizer lattice for every \(q\), and on the full subgroup lattice exactly when \(q\) is prime.
limitations: The group is the standard finite Heisenberg group over the finite field \(\mathbb F_q\).
The statement does not classify Chermak--Delgado lattices of arbitrary class-two or ring-Heisenberg groups.
